title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 63–68): Grothendieck is building a combinatorial 'analysis situs'. The ingredients are a set F of 'pieces' (faces or strata, and M when one passes to strata), a subset L ⊂ F of minimal elements, and a symmetric 'disjunction' relation ∥. A 'rapport' is a subset of F closed for the polarity A ↦ A^∥ = {G | G ∥ F for all F ∈ A}. The rapports form a complete lattice Σ_F with an orthocomplement ∁_F. On p. 66 he shows that Σ_F ≅ Σ_Λ for a suitable Λ ⊂ F, via the 'shadow' A ↦ omb_Λ(A) = A ∩ Λ. The best choice is Λ = L, provided axiom AtL2 holds. On pp. 63–64 he had worried that Σ need not behave like a Boolean algebra: A ⊂ B need not be equivalent to A ∩ ∁B = ∅, and distributivity can fail.

This page treats the 'particularly pleasant' case where ∥_L on L is just x ≠ y, as for quasi-set-theoretic structures.
- For any X ⊂ L we get X^∥ = L \ X and X^∥∥ = X. So every subset of L is closed and Σ_L = P(L), with ∁_L the ordinary set complement.
- The support of a part A of F (or of M), identified with a part of L, is simply its shadow: supp A = omb(A) := ∪_{F∈A} omb(F).
- The cosupport is cosupp A = L \ supp A.
- The reason is that the crucial disjunction relation becomes set-theoretic disjointness of shadows, F ∥ G ⇔ omb F ∩ omb G = ∅. The shadows are 'renamed supports for the occasion'.
- Hence the perplexities of pp. 63–64 dissolve. Σ is a Boolean algebra, so A ⊂ B ⇔ A ∧ ∁(B) = 0_Σ, and A ∧ ⋁_i B_i = ⋁_i (A ∧ B_i).

On p. 68 he generalises from L to any family P of 'points' that are pairwise disjoint and detect disjunction; then Σ ≅ P(P).
errors: No mathematical error. The equivalence F ∥ G ⇔ omb F ∩ omb G = ∅ tacitly uses the compatibility axiom (AtL2 from p. 66): disjunction of pieces is detected on minimal elements. The page does not restate this.
In the distributivity formula, ⋁ in Σ is the closure of the union. In the Boolean case P(L) this is just the union, so the formula is the ordinary distributive law, which holds.

ideas.what: Closed subsets ('rapports') for a symmetric disjunction relation, with orthocomplement; when the relation is ≠ the lattice is the full power set (Boolean).
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality spaces / polarity (Galois) closure; ortholattice of biorthogonally closed sets; the discrete orthogonality space gives the Boolean algebra P(X)

ideas.what: Support of a family of strata defined as the union of the shadows of its members on minimal strata; cosupport as the complement.
ideas.modern_name: Support in a stratified / cell-complex setting (union of minimal cells); open-star-type correspondences

ideas.what: Recognising that failure of 'A ⊂ B ⇔ A ∧ ∁B = 0' and of distributivity is the obstruction, and that it disappears when disjunction is set-theoretic.
ideas.modern_name: Orthomodularity/distributivity of ortholattices (quantum-logic phenomenon) versus Boolean case

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'rapports' defined by a disjunction relation, and his 'perplexities' about distributivity and about A ⊂ B vs A ∩ ∁B = ∅, are exactly the non-Boolean ortholattice phenomena of orthogonality spaces in quantum logic. He resolves them by the standard criterion that a discrete orthogonality gives a Boolean algebra. The parallel between his tame-topology foundations and quantum-logic lattice theory seems not to be noted in the literature on these notes, though mathematically it is elementary.
missed.quote: Dans ce cas, les perplexités p. 63, 64 se résolvent, on a A⊂B ⟺ A∩∁(B)=∅_Σ, A∩⋁B_i = ⋁A∩B_i dans Σ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historiographic. It situates the 1986 Analysis situs drafts relative to orthogonality-space and lattice-theoretic approaches to 'regions'. Those approaches include mereotopology and region-based topology, which are also built on a disjointness/contact relation.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean but elementary special case: the discrete orthogonality relation gives the power-set Boolean algebra. Its interest is only as a window on Grothendieck's unpublished combinatorial foundations of tame topology, and on his independent arrival at orthogonality-space lattice issues.
transcription_corrections: 'ouv_L(A) = ouv(A)' should read 'omb_L(A) = omb(A)' (ombre/shadow, consistent with p. 66); likewise in 'supp A = omb(A) ≝ ∪_{F∈A} omb(F)' and 'omb F ∩ omb G = ∅'.
'sur les ouvs (ouv.-options [?]) supports pour la circonstance' should read approximately 'sur les ombres (rebaptisées supports pour la circonstance)'.
The marginal reference is 'p. 63, 64', placed before 'se résolvent'.
'Ceci tient au fait que la relation cruciale de disjonction devient simplement' is confirmed by the image.
